The worker suffered a low back injury in July 1975 when he slipped 10 feet down a slope.  He returned to work in September 1975, but had a recurrence in March and April 1976.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Adjudicator denying further entitlement from December 1978 to January 1979.
The worker suffered a low back injury in September 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a recurrence in November 1991.

The worker's benefits were terminated in January 1993, when he refused work made available by the accident employer.  In January 1994, the Reinstatement Officer held that the work was unsuitable and granted the worker entitlement to vocational rehabilitation services, subsequent to January 1994, as well as temporary benefits from January 1993 until January 1994.  However, these benefits were reduced to the 50% level because the worker's self-directed vocational rehabilition plan was inadequate.  The worker appealed the Reinstatement Officer's decision.

DecKeywords: Dependency benefits (common law spouse); Dependency benefits (separation)
DecSummary: The worker died at work in August 1988.  The daughter of the worker received dependency benefits.  However, her mother, common law spouse, did not receive the worker's dependency benefits.  The spouse appealed.
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.  [3 pages]
A 41-year-old general labourer suffered a stroke at work.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement.

A nurses' aide suffered a low back and shoulder injury while lifting a patient in 1981.  She was awarded a 15% pension, increased to 20% for chronic pain in 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a s. 147(4) supplement.

DecKeywords: Delay (onset of symptoms); Disablement (nature of work)
DecSummary: A housekeeping aide suffered a right knee injury when she slipped and fell on ice in February 1990.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for left plantar fasciitis.

DecKeywords: Independent operator (truck driver); Right to sue
DecSummary: The issue in this s. 17 application was whether R was a worker or an independent operator.  R was employed as a truck driver by S Ltd until January 1993.  At that time, he entered into a lease/purchase arrangement with S Ltd for the acquisition of a tractor.  On the same date, R entered into an agreement to operate as a contractor to drive loads for S Ltd and registered a firm name.

The worker fell on a concrete floor in May 1989.  She continued to work for the day, and went to the hospital after work, where she was treated for bruises on her thigh and knee.  She returned to work the next day.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for low back and neck disability in 1992.
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.  [6 pages]

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer regarding ongoing benefits for an accident in 1991.  In this decision, the Panel determined whether the accident in 1991 was a new accident or a recurrence of prior compensable and non-compensable injuries.
The worker's estate appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for the worker's death at work by heart attack.
The worker appealed a decision of the Appeal Board denying entitlement for enucleation of the worker's right eye in 1978, which the worker claimed was related to an accident in 1962.
The worker suffered a low back strain when she slipped on ice in January 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying benefits after April 1992.

DecKeywords: Rehabilitation, vocational (training); Supplements, transitional provisions (temporary) (participation in rehabilitation); Temporary disability (beyond pension level)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back injury in 1984 for which he was awarded a 15% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying sponsorship in a community college program from 1989 to 1992 and a s. 147(2) supplement.  The worker also appealed denial of temporary benefits from June 1991 to January 1992.

The worker suffered foot injuries for which he was awarded a 16% pension.  The worker requested full commutation of the pension to invest in a trucking business.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting only a partial commutation in the amount of $10,000.  The worker stated that he wanted all or nothing.
The worker withdrew the appeal.  [2 pages]
The worker suffered a right knee injury, diagnosed as a torn meniscus and a torn anterior cruciate ligament.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a NEL award.
The employer's appeal was withdrawn at the employer's request.  [3 pages]

The worker suffered a left rotator cuff strain in January 1991.  He returned to modified work.  In May 1992, the worker laid off due to bilateral shoulder tendonitis.  The worker appealed denial of further benefits.
The worker suffered a back injury in 1979 and a recurrence in 1981.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further entitlement in 1986.

The worker suffered a wrist injury from repetitive lifting in November 1989.  She was awarded a 3% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for chronic pain.
The employer, a trucking business, was appealing a decision of the Hearings Officer as to a number of issues related to assessment.  The dispute generally centered on the status of owner/operators.

DecKeywords: Consequences of injury; Medical opinion (overuse syndrome); Overuse syndrome
DecSummary: The worker suffered a right shoulder disability within three months of beginning repetitive assembly line work in 1988.  When she returned to work in April 1989, she was struck on her right shoulder by a falling object.  The worker received benefits as a result of her right shoulder disability.  She was seeking benefits for a left shoulder disability that she attributed to overuse of her left arm due to her inability to use her right arm.  Surgery was performed on the worker's left shoulder in October 1993.
The worker died from compensable lung cancer in 1963.  His widow died in 1970.  The estate of the widow appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying dependency benefits to the widow.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a right wrist injury which the worker related to a compensable right elbow injury.  On the evidence, the application of a cast and subsequent physiotherapy for the right elbow injury aggravated a preexisting but asymptomatic non-compensable right wrist condition.

The worker was appealing the level of the NEL award for organic disability.  The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue entitlement for chronic pain and re-evaluation of his award based on deterioration of his condition.  [4 pages]

DecKeywords: Supplements, transitional provisions (benefit from rehabilitation) (earning capacity)
DecSummary: A skilled machine operator suffered a shoulder and neck injury in February 1988, for which he was awarded a 10% pension.  In November 1988, he returned to modified work, with assistance provided for heavy lifting, at no wage loss.  In January 1990, the worker was laid off by the employer for economic reasons.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying vocational rehabilitation and s. 147 supplementary benefits after January 1990.

On this appeal the employer asked the Tribunal to exercise its discretion to instruct the Board to re-open the NEER calculation pertaining to two claims.  In each case, the employer applied for SIEF relief a few months before the three year NEER cut-off date and the Board granted entitlement to such relief a few months after the cut-off date for such adjustments.

DecKeywords: Jurisdiction, Tribunal (right to sue) (initial entitlement); Out of province (substantial connection); Right to sue; Words and phrases (benefits payable)
DecSummary: The defendants in a court action applied for a declaration that the plaintiff's right of action was taken away by the Act.  The defendants were workers of Schedule 1 employers and were in the course of their employment at the time of the motor vehicle accident which was the subject of the court action.

DecKeywords: Benefit of the doubt; Temporary disability (beyond pension level)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision denying him entitlement to temporary total disability benefits subsequent to April 1993.  He twisted his low back at work in September 1988 while stepping off a tractor.  The worker sustained a disc protrusion at L3-4 and underwent a discotomy in June 1989.  He was awarded a 15% pension in September 1991.  In November 1992, the worker was awarded a provisional psychiatric pension for two years, retroactive to September 1991.  In April 1993 the worker's vocational rehabilitation file was closed and his temporary supplementary benefits under s. 147(2) were terminated.  The worker was diagnosed with rectal cancer in August 1993.  He died in January 1995.

The worker suffered a compensable injury in 1981 for which he was awarded a 10% pension.  The worker suffered a recurrence in 1986.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer regarding the earnings basis for calculation of benefits for the recurrence in 1986.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue a final decision at the Board for collateral issues which were inseparable from the narrow issue on the appeal.  [5 pages]

The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying retroactive manual adjustment of the employer's 1989 NEER calculation to account for SIEF relief granted after the expiry of the three-year NEER review period.

As a result of reporting error by the employer as to the worker's earnings, the worker received benefits based on an earnings basis that was too high.  There was an overpayment of about $5,500.  The Board started recovering the overpayment by deducting 10% of the worker's benefits.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer directing the continuing recovery of the overpayment.

A cutter in the forest industry suffered a laceration to his wrist in November 1974.  Due to recurring problems, he underwent surgery in 1984.  He was left with a permanent disability for which he was awarded a 12% pension.  He was unable to return to work in the forest industry.  The Board provided VR services from 1985 to May 1991, when the worker's file was closed.  It provided job search assistance followed by academic upgrading and further job search assistance.  In March 1992, the file was reopened and the worker retrained successfully as a truck driver.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying VR services and s. 147(2) supplementary benefits from May 1991 to March 1992.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying commutation of his 20% pension, valued at about $75,000, which the worker wanted for the purpose of starting his own business.

A plumber suffered neck and shoulder injuries in a compensable motor vehicle accident in July 1989. The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying s. 147(2) supplementary benefits from January 1994 to July 1994 and s. 147(4) benefits thereafter.

The worker was injured at work in January 1986 when he was driving a scoop tram down a hill over some loose muck, causing him to bounce in the air and land on the side of his air cushion seat spring.  He did not lose any time.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further entitlement in February 1992 when he lifted a snowmobile at home.

DecKeywords: Future economic loss {FEL} (deemed earnings); Future economic loss {FEL} (time periods); Issue setting; Procedure (moot issue); Waiver (right to compensation) (mediation)
DecSummary: The worker was injured in July 1990.  The Board originally discontinued benefits in December 1991 after finding that the worker refused suitable full-time work.  A few days later, she returned to part-time work.  On appeal, the Hearings Officer granted temporary wage loss benefits until February 1992.  In February 1992, the Board assessed the worker for a FEL award but found that she had no future economic loss.  The decision was effective as of April 1, 1992.  On April 3, 1992, the worker's employment was terminated due to shortage of work.  The worker appealed denial of temporary benefits after February 1992 and denial of a FEL award.  The worker also wanted the Panel to make a finding that the worker was entitled to VR services in April 1992.
The hearing was adjourned to await a final decision from the Board on related conditions.  [4 pages]

The worker suffered severe burns in 1988, for which he was awarded a 15% pension for organic disability and a 25% pension for psychotraumatic disability.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting only s. 147(4) supplementary benefits from November 1991 to May 1993.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to confirm the correct diagnosis of his condition.  [4 pages]

A long distance truck driver appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a heart attack which the worker claimed was caused by chronic stress.  The worker had been a truck driver for 23 years.  He began employment with the accident employer about October 1991, and suffered the heart attack in January 1993.  The worker claimed that, after he had been working for about six months, the employer started asking the worker to perform acts which were contrary to various rules and laws, such as falsifying log books and breaking bonding seals.

DecKeywords: Rehabilitation (reassessment of negative decision); Rehabilitation, vocational (considering self totally disabled)
DecSummary: The worker strained his back in July 1989.  He had  worked for 12 years in the construction industry.  After six weeks of physiotherapy, beginning in September 1991, it was suggested that the worker return to work with restrictions of no lifting above five pounds and no repetitive bending.  In November 1991 the worker returned to work with the accident employer on a work hardening program but stopped after a few days and claimed to be totally disabled.  The worker requested additional vocational rehabilitation services in February 1992.  When the worker met with his caseworker, in March 1992, to discuss rehabilitation services and the availability of modified work, the worker advised that he did not feel capable of working at that time.  He was awarded a 10% pension in 1993, but with no supplement as he was claiming to be totally disabled.  The worker appealed a decision denying him additional rehabilitation services.

The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying manual adjustment of the employer's NEER record to include SIEF relief granted after closure of the three-year window for NEER adjustments.

A construction worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a back injury which the worker claimed he suffered at work on the day he was being laid off due to shortage of work.

DecKeywords: Future economic loss {FEL} (sustainability award); Future economic loss {FEL} (time periods); Suitable employment (deemed earnings) (prospects for rehabilitation)
DecSummary: A 28-year-old powder mixer suffered a left hand injury in June 1990 when his hand was caught in the gears of a machine.  The injury caused the partial amputation of two fingers.  The worker returned to modified work as a press operator in April 1991.  In August 1991, he was laid off.  In March 1992, he was awarded a 4% NEL award but a FEL award was denied.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer confirming denial of the FEL award.

DecKeywords: Silicosis; Medical opinion (respiratory disease) (respiratory infection); Occupational Disease Panel (respiratory disease); Pneumonia
DecSummary: The worker's widow appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying benefits for the worker's death in 1987 from pneumonia.  The worker was a gold miner from 1933 to 1962.  He was awarded a 30% pension for silicosis.  The widow claimed that the pneumonia was related to the silicosis.

The worker suffered a shoulder injury in January 1991.  The Board arranged for the worker to return to work in November 1991, but she stopped working again after two weeks.  Originally, the Board found that the worker was not available for suitable work.  On appeal, the Board concluded that the work was not suitable.  The Board granted temporary benefits until March 26, 1992, when it found that she did not make a concerted effort to find work.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits after March 26, 1992, and denying s. 147 supplementary benefits.

The worker suffered a herniated disc in September 1988.  He was awarded a 30% pension for organic disability.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a psychiatric disability and denying vocational rehabilitation services and a s. 147(2) supplement after June 1992.
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer, except for a number of personal references which were not relevant.  [5 pages]

The worker suffered back injuries in 1978 and 1985, for which he was awarded a 10% pension, increased to 25% in May 1990.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying full temporary benefits from December 1989 to June 1990.

DecKeywords: Access to worker file, statutory; Procedure (absent parties)
DecSummary: The hearing of this s. 71 appeal proceeded by way of conference call in the absence of the worker.  There were written submissions from the worker.  The Panel had sufficient information to make an informed decision.

DecKeywords: Consequences of injury (residual weakness); Subsequent incidents (outside work)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a back and hip injury in 1979.  In September 1990, he fell down stairs at home.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying benefits for the accident at home and denying s. 147 benefits after the worker was laid off in November 1991.

DecKeywords: Suitable employment (suitable for worker's capabilities) (personal characteristics of worker)
DecSummary: A miner suffered a low back injury in January 1990.  He returned to modified work in the gatehouse in July 1990.  After an unsuccessful attempt at regular work in February 1993, he returned again to work in the gatehouse.  In March 1993, the employer eliminated all gatehouse positions.  The employer offered the worker a job as a security guard, which the worker refused.  The Board granted 50% temporary benefits from March 1993 to July 1993 and no benefits thereafter.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further temporary benefits.

DecKeywords: Supplements, transitional provisions (benefit from rehabilitation); Temporary disability (beyond pension level)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back injury in 1973 for which he was awarded a 20% pension, increased to 30% in 1981 and to 40% in 1993.  The worker had a further period of temporary total disability in September 1989.  In April 1991, he was found fit for modified work and started receiving his pension and a supplement under s. 147(2).  In June 1992, he started, but did not complete, an eight-week work assessment.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits or s. 147(2) supplementary benefits after June 1992.
The hearing of the worker's appeal was adjourned and the Panel directed Tribunal counsel to arrange for the attendance of a second employer.  [4 pages]

The worker was appealing granting of only 50% benefits for temporary partial disability during a specific period.  The appeal was withdrawn after the Panel explained the downside risk that the worker could lose the 50% benefits that he had received.  [4 pages]

The hearing of the worker's appeal regarding the level of his current permanent disability was adjourned and the matter referred to the Board for a reassessment.  Another issue was withdrawn.  [4 pages]
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.  [6 pages]

The employer appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer finding that the employer breached its re-employment obligations.  At the time the worker was injured, the worker was performing light work.  He had been performing this light work for a year due to a non-compensable condition.  After the accident, the employer notified the worker that light work would no longer be available and that, due to a corporate reorganization, all workers in his grade were being laid off.

The worker suffered shoulder and neck injuries when he was struck by a falling object in October 1990.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits after August 1992, denying further vocational rehabilitation services and denying a FEL award.

DecKeywords: Procedure (absent parties); Re-employment (termination) (contract worker); Transfer of costs (overpayment) (federal worker)
DecSummary: The worker was an orderly at a hospital run by a federal government department.  He was employed under term contracts, the last of which was scheduled to run from May 1992 to December 1992.  He was injured in August 1992, and returned to work in October 1992.  The employer did not renew his contract when it expired in December 1992.  The employer appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer finding that the employer breached its obligation to re-employ, levying a 50% penalty and granting benefits for two months.
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.  [3 pages]
The employer's appeal was withdrawn at the employer's request after a discussion with the Panel.  [3 pages]
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.  [3 pages]

The employer appealed a decision that it had failed to fulfil its re-employment obligations.  The employer's position was that it had terminated the worker's employment due to theft of company property and not for any reason related to his compensable injury.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue further entitlement at the Board.  [4 pages]

The worker suffered a low back injury in August 1987 and returned to work in September 1987.  He suffered a recurrence in February 1988 and his employment was terminated upon his return to work in March 1988.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further VR services after December 1992.
The Board increased the worker's pension from 15% to 40% retroactive to February 1983.  The worker appealed denial of payment of arrears to 1977.

DecKeywords: Re-employment (duration of obligation); Re-employment (obligation to re-employ) (commencement)
DecSummary: In March 1992, the worker began to experience a gradual onset of wrist pain.  The employer gave the worker modified work but no report was filed with the Board.  In October 1993, the worker's employment was terminated.  In November 1993, the worker claimed benefits for carpal tunnel syndrome.  In April 1994, the claim was allowed and temporary benefits were granted.  The worker appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer finding that the re-employment provisions of s. 54 did not apply in this case since the employer's obligation to re-employ had expired.

A 63-year-old worker suffered a right hip injury in July 1990.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits after July 1991 and denying a permanent impairment assessment.

DecKeywords: Benefit of the doubt; Disc, degeneration; Medical report (payment for)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back strain while pulling a cover off a carpet in 1978.  In 1980, he was awarded a 10% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for back surgery in 1992.

The employer appealed a decision granting the worker benefits for a recurrence.  The employer was to have been represented at the hearing by the assistant to one of its vice-presidents.  The employer's representative did not appear at the time scheduled for the hearing.  TCO contacted the employer by telephone and was told that the employer's representative ceased her employment with the employer about five months before the scheduled hearing.  The person with whom TCO spoke requested an adjournment.
The worker suffered a hernia in August 1983.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a low back condition and denying benefits for two periods.

The worker was struck on the head in 1972 by a heavy falling object.  He was wearing a hard hat and did not lose any time from work.  Over the years, the worker began to experience neck, shoulder and throat problems.  The Board granted entitlement for the neck and shoulder but denied entitlement for the throat problems.  The worker appealed denial of entitlement for the throat condition.
The Panel clarified Decision No. 569/95 by noting that it confirmed the Board's original FEL determination and directed that the Board review the R1 FEL determination.  [3 pages]
The worker suffered a compensable injury for which he received benefits for a period of time.  The worker was appealing denial of entitlement for chronic pain.

The employer appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer finding that the worker was entitled to sponsorship for upgrading to grade 12 equivalency and to full temporary benefits in September and October 1993.
The worker's request to reconsider Decision No. 775/95 was denied.  [4 pages]

DecKeywords: Suitable employment; Supplements, transitional provisions (temporary) (participation in rehabilitation); Worker (long term service)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a knee injury in May 1988.  He returned to modified work but stopped working again 10 days later.  The worker was assessed for a pension in September 1990.  He returned to work for the accident employer in June 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits from June 1990 to September 1990, and s. 147(2) supplementary benefits from September 1990 to June 1991.
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer, except for a reference which was not relevant.

DecKeywords: Chronic pain; Future economic loss {FEL} (deemed earnings); Rehabilitation, vocational (considering self totally disabled); Rehabilitation, vocational (suitability of program) (opinion of Board)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision granting her a zero FEL award.  Her job involved handling linen for a company that supplied linen to hospitals.  The worker, aged 54, strained her back while pushing a cart in May 1990.  Except for a few hours in February 1991, when she attempted very light work provided by the accident employer, the worker had not returned to work since the accident.  The Board recognized that the worker was suffering from chronic pain syndrome and depression and on this basis granted the worker a 25% NEL award.
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.  [3 pages]

The worker suffered a low back injury in May 1990.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for chronic pain.  On the evidence, the worker had pain inconsistent with organic findings.  There was a marked life disruption in occupational, social and home life.

DecKeywords: Rehabilitation, vocational (academic upgrading); Supplements, transitional provisions (benefit from rehabilitation)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision which denied him ongoing entitlement to supplementary benefits under section 147(2), from May 1992 onwards, on the basis that he was not likely to benefit from vocational rehabilitation services that would help to increase his earning capacity to approximate his pre-injury earnings.

DecKeywords: Availability for employment (job search); Rehabilitation, vocational (aid in getting worker back to work)
DecSummary: The worker suffered accidents in 1980 and 1984 for which he was receiving pensions.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer confirming denial of VR services after 1991.

DecKeywords: Significant contribution (of compensable accident to ongoing condition)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision denying her benefits for a neck condition on the basis that her ongoing impairment did not result from an April 1987 work accident, but rather was the consequence of pre-existing non-compensable problems, complicated by a traumatic event in October 1987.  The worker related her neck problems to repetitive overhead lifting at work in April 1987.  The worker did not report the accident at the time and did not lay off work until January 1991.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a giant cell tumour of the tendon sheath of the right thumb.  Evidence did not support a finding that the condition was related to the worker's repetitive work.

In August 1991 the worker strained her back and neck while unloading boxes.  She was slinging lighter boxes fairly quickly when she lifted a substantially heavier box and felt immediate pain across her shoulders and down her back.  Based on evidence of preexisting back problems, the Board accepted entitlement on an aggravation basis.  Three weeks later, the Board concluded that the worker had reached her pre-accident state and terminated temporary benefits.  The worker sought ongoing temporary benefits as well as entitlement to a permanent impairment award.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for fibromyalgia which the worker claimed was related to his exposure to cold working conditions while at work maintaining an ice rink.

A part-time clerk was injured in September 1992.  In January 1993, she returned to alternative employment at no wage loss as a cashier.  In September 1993, her job changed in a material way.  She was unable to continue with the job.  Her employment was terminated in December 1993.  The employer appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer finding that it breached its re-employment obligations and imposing a penalty.
The worker suffered a low back strain in July 1986.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a pension assessment.
The worker tripped and fell on both knees in February 1987.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further entitlement in 1992 for right knee disability.

DecKeywords: Board Directives and Guidelines (interest); Discretion, Board (interest) (fettering); Interest; Merits and justice
DecSummary: A jack leg driller suffered from severe white finger disease, resulting in amputation of a number of fingers in the early 1980s.  By 1982, he began suffering leg symptoms but entitlement for this condition was initially denied.  In 1985, the worker committed suicide.  Dependency benefits were initially denied.  These decisions were confirmed by the Decision Review Specialist in 1987.  In the early 1990s, the worker applied for reconsideration of those decisions.  In June 1992, the Decision Review Specialist granted entitlement for vascular disease in the legs.  In November 1992, the Decision Review Specialist granted dependency benefits on the basis that the worker's death was attributable to his compensable disability.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying interest on these benefits.

A health care aide suffered a shoulder injury in 1989 for which she was awarded a 3% pension.  She returned to modified work four months later.  In February 1990, the worker switched from full-time to part-time modified work so that she could take community college courses to qualify as a lab technician.  The worker enrolled in these courses without seeking Board approval.  She did not know at the time that the Board provides VR services to sponsor educational programs.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying reimbursement for the cost of tuition.

DecKeywords: Chronic pain; Delay (onset of symptoms); Disability (disabled from working)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a shoulder injury in December 1990 and received benefits until September 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for chronic pain and denying benefits after September 1992.

The worker was appealing a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further temporary benefits.  The appeal was adjourned to await a final decision from the Board on the issue of permanent disability.  [4 pages]

The worker suffered a shoulder injury in October 1989.  The worker suffered further shoulder pain at home in March 1992 while throwing out some garbage.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement in 1992.

DecKeywords: Intervening causes (conduct of worker); Misconduct; Subsequent incidents (outside work)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a knee injury for which he was receiving a pension.  In a subsequent incident outside work, the worker's knee gave out as he was working at a table saw at his workshop in his home.  When his knee gave out, his hand fell on to the blade of the saw.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for the hand injury.
The worker suffered a left shoulder injury in January 1986.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying full temporary benefits from July 1987 to November 1987.

DecKeywords: Adjournment (additional issues); Suitable employment; Consequences of injury (residual weakness); Credibility (interested witness)
DecSummary: A cashier suffered left hand-wrist tendinitis in July 1991.  She returned to modified work in November 1992 but stopped working again in December 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for right hand/wrist disability and denying further entitlement for left hand/wrist disability.

DecKeywords: In the course of employment (proceeding to and from work) (employer's vehicle)
DecSummary: An engineer for a public utilities commission was injured while travelling from his home to the construction project site on which he was working.  He had a company car which he also used for travelling to and from work.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer finding that the worker was in the course of employment at the time he was injured.
The worker suffered a back injury in 1989 for which she was awarded a 15% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying full benefits after January 1993.

DecKeywords: Adjournment (peremptory hearing date); Adjournment (representative availability); Procedure (absent parties)
DecSummary: In Decision No. 231/95I, the hearing of a s. 71 appeal was adjourned since the worker's representative was only prepared to argue a jurisdictional issue (which had already been decided a number of times on other appeals in which this representative appeared) and not the merits of the appeal.
The worker's appeal was withdrawn at the request of the worker.  [3 pages]

DecKeywords: Dependants (separation); In the course of employment (takes self out of employment) (intoxication); In the course of employment (travelling)
DecSummary: The worker was killed in a motor vehicle accident.  The worker was intoxicated at the time.  The worker's widow appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement.

DecKeywords: Chronic pain; Downside risk; Overpayment; Supplements, temporary
DecSummary: The worker suffered a back injury when she fell at work in December 1984.  She returned to work at the end of May 1985 but stopped work again a few days later.  In 1992, she was awarded a 10% pension for chronic pain retroactive to March 27, 1986.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting only 50% benefits for temporary partial disability from June 1985 to March 27, 1986, and denying temporary supplementary benefits from then to July 26, 1989.

The worker fell on an icy parking lot in March 1989.  She sustained a fracture of the humerus of her left arm.  She was awarded a 5% pension for her shoulder and arm.  The worker sought benefits for back, neck and psychotraumatic disabilities which she related to the same accident.
On consent, decision-making on this appeal was deferred for 60 days to allow the worker to decide whether to withdraw or proceed with the appeal.  [3 pages]

The worker suffered a neck and shoulder strain in August 1987 and received benefits until February 1988.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer confirming a 0% award for chronic pain.

The worker suffered a low back injury in December 1990.  The worker appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer denying vocational rehabilitation assistance after September 1993.  On the evidence, the worker was enrolled in  a 24-week academic upgrading program.  He showed a lack of commitment through his continued, increasing and unexplained absences.
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.  [3 pages]

DecKeywords: Psychotraumatic disability; Significant contribution (of compensable accident to psychological condition)
DecSummary: An autoworker suffered a back injury for which he was awarded a 10% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for psychotraumatic disability.

The worker was unrepresented at his appeal.  Shortly before the hearing, his representative had contacted him to inform him that legal aid had not been approved for the appeal.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue further matters at the Board.  [3 pages]

The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting entitlement for an accident.  The worker, a roofer, claimed that he slid a distance of 12 feet down a roof.  There were inconsistencies in the worker's evidence as well as in the evidence of a co-worker.  Also, the worker continued working for a number of days.

The worker suffered low back injuries for which he was receiving a pension.  He took early retirement in 1984 at age 55.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a s. 147(4) supplement.

The worker was appealing denial of temporary benefits for a period in 1991 and 1992.  The Panel brought to the worker's attention that, due to the different methods of calculation temporary and permanent benefits, the worker's pension was about three times greater that what he would receive with full temporary benefits.

The worker sought benefits for a low back disability subsequent to 1990.  He suffered a compensable low back injury in 1968 when he fell seven feet to the ground.  He received benefits for one month.  The evidence indicated that the worker sustained a low back injury at work in 1973.  The worker claimed that he received compensation benefits for this injury but neither he, the employer nor the Board had any record of that.

DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back injury in August 1990.  He could not return to his pre-accident employment.  The Board sponsored the worker in educational upgrading but, in May 1993, the school discontinued his studies due to poor progress and attendance.  The Board then arranged for a six-month work trial in a clerical position, but the worker stopped work on the first day.  the worker appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer denying VR services and supplementary benefits under s. 43(9) after June 1993.

The worker suffered a compensable back injury in January 1988.  He returned to modified work in March 1989.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further entitlement from January 1990 to November 1990.

The worker suffered a shoulder injury in 1986.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further benefits in 1991.

DecKeywords: Commutation (debt liquidation); Pensions (lump sum) (amalgamation of claims)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying commutation of her 5% pension for right elbow disability, valued at about $10,000, which the worker wanted for the purpose of debt liquidation.
The worker suffered a back injury in June 1991, and received benefits until September 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further benefits.

An application to reconsider Decision No. 98/95 was granted in part.  In Decision No. 98/95, the Panel calculated an amount of entitlement for the worker's spouse but declined to award interest.  There were no grounds to conclude that the amount of benefits was inappropriate.  However, the Panel was satisfied that Board policy reflected a non-discretionary approach to payment of interest and that, accordingly, interest should be paid from January 6, 1989.  [4 pages]

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (good reason to doubt correctness) (consideration of evidence)
DecSummary: The worker applied for leave to appeal a decision of the Appeal Board denying entitlement for disability in 1972 which the worker claimed was related to an accident in 1971.

DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying payment of his 10% pension, valued at about $54,000, as a lump sum.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue entitlement for chronic pain.  [4 pages]

DecKeywords: Natural justice (opportunity to make submissions); Parties (participation) (unrepresented party) (conduct)
DecSummary: As the Panel was making preliminary decisions regarding the procedure for hearing the worker's appeal and a number of other related appeals by the worker, the unrepresented worker became extremely abusive, packing up his materials and repeatedly swearing at the Panel.

DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back strain when he slipped in June 1989.  He also had a recurrence in September 1989.  In December 1990, he was awarded a 10% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits after December 1990 and confirming the level of the pension.

The worker suffered a low back injury in February 1986, and received benefits for 11 months.  He also received benefits for periods in 1987 and 1988.  In June 1989, he was awarded a 15% pension.  In August 1989, the worker had a further period of back disability in an incident outside work when the worker was changing a tire on his truck.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits in 1989.

DecKeywords: Access to worker file, statutory (employer); Access to worker file, statutory (issue in dispute) (FEL); Access to worker file, statutory (issue in dispute) (relevance) (new information)

The worker's request to reconsider Decision No. 353/95 was denied.  The worker's request was based on a number of grounds, including the presence of Tribunal counsel, the conduct of the hearing by the Vice-Chair and the presence on the hearing panel of a blind panel member.

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (good reason to doubt correctness) (natural justice)
DecSummary: The worker applied for leave to appeal a decision of the Appeal Board denying further entitlement in 1979 for inability to work which the worker related to a compensable accident in 1977.

DecKeywords: Access to worker file, statutory (issue in dispute) (NEL)
DecSummary: Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.  The documents were relevant to the issue in dispute of entitlement to a NEL award.  [5 pages]

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a back condition in July 1988 which the worker related to a minor compensable accident in April 1988 or to a second accident which the worker claimed he suffered in June 1988.
The worker suffered a knee injury in 1987.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for knee surgery in 1991.
The hearing of the worker's appeal was adjourned.  The case was not ready for hearing.  The Panel gave directions regarding further preparations.  [4 pages]

The worker suffered a back injury in a fall at work in September 1983.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further benefits in 1990.  Considering lack of continuity of treatment, the Panel found that the worker's condition in 1990 was not related to the 1983 accident.

The worker suffered a right foot injury in August 1990 when a pallet was accidentally lowered on his foot.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a NEL award, leading to the termination of VR assistance and FEL supplementary benefits.

An auto worker suffered a torn meniscus in March 1993.  He continued to perform strenuous work for one month until his condition was identified.  The employer then provided clerical work.  The worker performed the clerical work for two days then stopped working, claiming that the clerical work was not suitable since there was excessive walking required from the parking lot to the office and since he had to climb stairs to go to the washroom.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying full temporary benefits for three weeks after he stopped the clerical work.
The hearing was adjourned to allow the parties an opportunity to investigate an issue identified by the Panel.  [3 pages]
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue further matters at the Board.  [3 pages]

A worker suffered a compensable injury in March 1989.  On September 10, 1992, the employer applied for SIEF relief.  The application was denied on September 22, 1992.  The employer disputed the decision.  On March 2, 1993, the employer was granted 50% SIEF relief.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a retroactive adjustment to the employer's 1989 NEER assessment.

A seamstress received benefits for right shoulder tendonitis beginning in April 1989.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer finding that modified work offered by the employer in December 1991 was not suitable and that, accordingly, the worker was entitled to further temporary benefits.

The worker appealed a decision denying her supplementary benefits under s. 147(4).  The worker was employed as a cashier when she injured her back in April 1988.  She had not returned to work since then.  The worker was denied supplementary benefits on the basis that she was only willing to work part-time.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue a final decision at the Board regarding entitlement for chronic pain.  [3 pages]

The employer sought the re-opening of NEER calculations for the purpose of adjusting the costs of two claims in which the Board granted the employer entitlement to SIEF relief shortly after the cut-off date for such adjustments.

In 1979, the worker suffered an accident in which he fractured two front teeth.  Posts and crowns were placed on the teeth.  In 1989, the worker was struck on the head by a falling pipe.  In 1990, one of the teeth injured in 1979 had to be removed and replaced with a permanent bridge.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting entitlement for the bridge in 1990.

The worker appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer denying a FEL supplement from June 1993 to April 1994.  In June 1993, the employer offered modified work which was not suitable for the worker.  The worker then conducted an aggressive job search on his own which was successful.  Continuation of vocational rehabilitation services would have been of benefit to the worker.

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (substantial new evidence) (medical report)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a back injury in 1978 and a thumb injury in 1980.  The worker applied for leave to appeal a decision of the Appeal Board denying entitlement for further back disability in 1980.

DecKeywords: Rehabilitation (aid in getting worker back to work) (self-employment); Transfer of costs
DecSummary: The worker suffered an arm injury in 1983.  The Board sponsored the worker in a retraining program that was completed in May 1990.  VR services were closed in August 1991, at which time the worker was still without a job.  The worker pursued an opportunity at self-employment.  The worker appealed the decision terminating VR services.

The worker suffered left shoulder and neck injuries in June 1989.  He was assessed for a pension in April 1991 and July 1991, but, on both assessments, it was found that he had no permanent impairment.  He was informed in May 1991 that temporary benefits were being terminated but continued to receive temporary benefits through Board error until September 1991, creating an overpayment of $6,000.  He suffered a recurrence in November 1991 and received full benefits until January 1992 and 50% from January 1992 to March 1993.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a pension, granting only 50% benefits from January 1992 to March 1993, and refusing to waive the overpayment.

The employer appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer granting sponsorship to the worker for academic upgrading and training.  The worker was not present for the hearing and his representative could not explain his absence.

The worker suffered a compensable injury in 1969.  In 1992, he was awarded a 10% pension retroactive to 1988, later made retroactive to the date of the accident.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer regarding the earnings basis for calculation of the pension.
A steelworker was receiving benefits for lung cancer.  He appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for chronic obstructive lung disease.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a partial commutation of his pension.  The pension was valued at about $124,000.  The worker wanted to commute one-third of the pension for the purpose of buying a motor vehicle in order to work as a courier.

The worker sought additional vocational rehabilitation assistance.  From January 1987 to August 1987, the worker underwent a general upgrading program at a community college.  He started a two year electronic program in September 1987.  It was subsequently agreed that the worker would attend an additional year in an instrumentation program.  In the autumn of 1991 the worker still had not completed the program and advised that he was unable to attend school because his leg gave out on him on the stairs, resulting in an aggravation of his compensable back condition.  The worker's vocational rehabilitation services were terminated in November 1991 for failure to cooperate by not fulfilling the commitments undertaken under the vocational rehabilitation plan.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue a final decision from the Board regarding chronic pain.  [3 pages]
The worker suffered a back and shoulder injury in June 1988.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer regarding benefits after April 1989.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a back condition which the worker related to the nature of her work.  The worker was not a credible witness.  There were inconsistencies in her evidence.  The Panel concluded that the worker did not injure her back at work.

The worker suffered a cervical strain in April 1991.  The Board terminated benefits in June 1992 after finding that the worker refused suitable employment.  On appeal, this decision was reversed by the Hearings Officer.  The employer appealed.

The employer sought a retroactive adjustment to its 1989 NEER assessment.  The worker injured his back in May 1989, but he returned to work in November 1989.  After several months, the worker claimed a recurrence and received further benefits from July 1990 to June 1991.  Following the recurrence, the employer took more active steps in support of its position that there were grounds for SIEF relief.  The Board denied the employer's request for SIEF relief in December 1991.  The employer then requested access to the worker's WCB claim file.  The employer did not receive access until June 1992.  The employer then renewed its request for SIEF relief which was granted in October 1992.
The worker fell from a ladder in November 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying benefits after June 1993.

DecKeywords: Rehabilitation, vocational (job search); Supplements, transitional provisions (wage loss)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision denying him s. 147 supplementary benefits and vocational rehabilitation benefits beyond July 1992.  The worker was self-employed from 1975 to May 1988 as the owner of a travel agency.  He injured his low back while picking up a pencil in May 1988.  He was awarded a 10% pension in 1989.  In June 1989 the worker began employment as a weigh master with a municipality.  On his first day on this job he fell while attempting to sit on a stool and injured his shoulder and face.  No physical restrictions were found to have resulted from the 1989 accident.  However, the worker did not return to work and he was eventually granted a 15% chronic pain disability pension in June 1992, retroactive to June 1989.

DecKeywords: Available employment; Future economic loss {FEL} (sustainability award); Future economic loss {FEL} (time periods)
DecSummary: A carpenter suffered a knee injury in September 1990.  In December 1991, the Board closed his VR file after concluding that he was capable of modified work but was claiming total disability.  In January 1992, a FEL adjudicator concluded that the worker was entitled to a zero FEL award.  In June 1992, the worker found other work.  The Hearings Officer found that it was questionable whether the worker could have sustained even modified work in the construction industry.  The Hearings Officer granted a 1% FEL sustainability award.  The worker appealed the decision to grant only a 1% award.
A 28-year-old worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for hearing loss.

A supply teacher suffered a knee injury when she was assaulted on June 2, 1992, while doing yard duty.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits after June 10, 1992.

DecKeywords: In the course of employment (sidewalk); Right to sue
DecSummary: The defendant in a civil case applied to determine whether the plaintiff's right of action was taken away.  The plaintiff slipped on an icy public sidewalk while proceeding from the employer's parking lot to the entrance to the employer's premises.  The issue was whether the plaintiff was in the course of employment at the time of the accident.

The worker suffered an injury to his right testicle in 1991, diagnosed as epididymitis and hydrocele.  He underwent a hydrocelectomy in July 1991 to drain excess fluid in the scrotum.  The worker underwent a second hydrocelectomy in 1993.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement in 1993.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue entitlement for another condition at the Board.

DecKeywords: Jurisdiction, Tribunal (stay of proceedings); Procedure (stay of proceedings)
DecSummary: In a pre-hearing conference, the employer argued that the worker's appeal should be stayed pending resolution of proceedings brought by the worker to the Ontario Human Rights Commission.
The worker was a truck driver in the forestry business.  He suffered a compensable injury in December 1990.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a FEL award.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue entitlement for fibromyalgia at the Board.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue entitlement for non-organic disability at the Board.  [3 pages]

The worker's appeal was considered withdrawn in the absence of the worker.  The worker had not informed the Tribunal or his own representative prior to the hearing that he would not be attending.  The representative did not have authorization to proceed.  [3 pages]
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying commutation of his pension for the purpose of business investment.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer deducting the full amount of his benefits under the Canada Pension Plan from the amount he is likely to be able to earn in suitable and available employment, for purposes of determining his FEL award.  The worker submitted that, pursuant to s. 43(7)(b), the Board should have regard to CPP benefits and that the Board should consider such benefits only as a factor to assist in the determination of the worker's likely earnings.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue entitlement for chronic pain.  [3 pages]

The worker was injured in a fall in October 1991.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying benefits after March 1992.  On the evidence, the worker continued to be disabled by organic and non-organic disability.  He reached maximal medical rehabilitation by January 1993.

The worker suffered a compensable injury in January 1976 and returned to work in November 1976.  The worker laid off in April 1993, and was awarded a 10% pension in May 1995.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits from April 1993 to May 1995.

DecKeywords: Supplements, transitional provisions (increase in earning capacity)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a back injury in 1986 for which she was awarded a pension.  The worker retrained as a youth worker and obtained employment.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a s. 147(4) supplement.

The worker suffered an acute respiratory condition as a result of workplace exposure to fumes.  The Board granted entitlement for this condition but denied entitlement for a back condition.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer confirming denial of entitlement for the back condition.

DecKeywords: Jurisdiction, Tribunal (medical examination) (further order); Medical examination (employer request)
DecSummary: The employer applied for an order directing the worker to attend a medical examination by an orthopaedic specialist.  The employer had a valid compensation goal as the suitability of modified work.  However, the Panel was not satisfied that an orthopaedic specialist would be able to resolve the fundamental differences between the parties as to the nature of suitable work.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for physical and psychiatric disability which the worker related to unleaded gasoline through exhaust, liquid and vapour.  The Panel required additional expert evidence.  The Panel directed Tribunal counsel to obtain an opinion from a Tribunal medical assessor.  [13 pages]

The worker suffered multiple soft tissue injuries when he slipped and fell backwards in August 1992.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further temporary benefits for organic disability after August 1993 and denying entitlement for chronic pain.

DecKeywords: Jurisdiction, Tribunal (final decision of Board) (parties of record); Notice of hearing (owner/operators)
DecSummary: The employer was appealing a decision of the Hearings Officer that its owner/operators were considered workers of the employer for the purposes of the Act, for the period from January 1992 to July 1993.  In this interim decision, the Panel had to determine whether the owner/operators were entitled to notice of the proceedings.

DecKeywords: Future economic loss {FEL} (deemed earnings); Future economic loss {FEL} (review); Future economic loss {FEL} (time periods)
DecSummary: A welder suffered a low back injury in July 1990.  In May 1992, the Board granted a 43% FEL award based on deemed earnings of $10 per hour as a security guard.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying an increase in the FEL award.

DecKeywords: Continuing entitlement; Medical report (opinion of treating doctor preferred); Strains and sprains (cervical) (cervical pain syndrome)
DecSummary: The worker sustained a compensable accident in, January 1990, while lifting a propane tank.  He appealed a Hearings Officer decision terminating his benefits in May 1990.  The worker's complaints varied from the upper back, to the shoulder, to the neck, to the low back.  The Panel accepted the opinion of one of the worker's treating specialists.  He diagnosed cervical pain syndrome whereby the initial injury occurred in the key site, a spot in the front of the lower neck, from where pain was referred to the other areas about which the worker complained.

The worker suffered a compensable injury in March 1989.  The Board granted 50% SIEF relief to the employer in October 1989.  In March 1991, the employer applied for greater SIEF relief.  In November 1992, the Board increased SIEF relief to 75%.  The employer was subject to NEER.  Since the three-year window for reviewing the accident experience for accidents in 1989 had expired, the Board refused to re-open the NEER accounting to reflect the added SIEF relief.  The employer appealed.

The worker suffered from a respiratory condition for which he was receiving a 9% pension.  The Hearings Officer increased the pension to 37% retroactive to June 1989.  The worker appealed denial of payment of the increase retroactive to 1986.

DecKeywords: Discretion, Board (application industries); Estoppel; Personal coverage (estimated earnings); Schedule 1 employer (application industries)
DecSummary: A husband and wife were partners in a hairstyling business.  The wife was denied benefits with respect to an accident reported in April 1993, on the basis that the business was not a Schedule 1 employer at that time.

The worker suffered low back, shoulder and neck injuries in an accident in 1980.  He was awarded a pension for low back disability.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further entitlement for shoulder and neck disability.

DecKeywords: Brain damage; Cognitive impairment; Headaches; Significant contribution (of compensable accident to disability)
DecSummary: The worker was a chef.  A pot that he was taking from a shelf fell on his head.  He returned to work after one week.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further entitlement for headaches and cognitive and behavioural problems.

A worker of a paving company went into a retail store to buy a part for a machine.  He slipped on paint which had fallen onto the floor of the store.  The paving company appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer refusing to transfer the costs of the accident to the retail store.

DecKeywords: Future economic loss {FEL} (eligibility) (disability); Issue setting; Re-employment (non-compliance) (mitigation by worker); Rehabilitation, vocational (academic training); Supplements, FEL; Temporary partial benefits (level of benefits)
DecSummary: In October 1991, the worker, who was a cook, fell while carrying a one hundred pound side of beef and injured his back.  In August 1993 the Board recognized that the worker had a permanent impairment in the thoracolumbar spine.  The worker was granted an 11% NEL award.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue further entitlement at the Board.  [4 pages]
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for right elbow epicondylitis.  On the evidence, the worker's condition was due to the repetitive nature of her work.

DecKeywords: Rehabilitation, vocational (academic upgrading); Rehabilitation, vocational (benefit from rehabilitation)
DecSummary: A 30-year-old worker was a fifth-year apprentice electrician when he was injured in 1990.  Under Board auspices, he obtained his electrician's license and took a program in creative job search techniques.  The worker appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer denying sponsorship in academic upgrading to obtain his grade 12 diploma.

DecKeywords: Expenses (lost salary); Supplements, transitional provisions (temporary) (participation in rehabilitation)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back injury in July 1989 for which he was awarded a 10% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a s. 147(2) supplement after April 1993.

DecSummary: A truck driver and a taxi driver were killed in a motor vehicle accident.  Both drivers were workers of Schedule 1 employers and were in the course of employment at the time of the accident.  The dependants of the truck driver brought an action against the person who was the sole shareholder, director and executive officer of the taxi company that employed the taxi driver.  The defendant was also the owner of the taxi driven by the taxi driver.  The plaintiffs applied to determine whether the right of action was taken away.
The hearing was adjourned so that the complete clinical notes of four doctors could be obtained.  [3 pages]

The hearing was adjourned so that clarification could be obtained from the Board as to the terms of the decision which was under appeal.  The worker had been receiving treatment outside Canada since 1980 and there were problems reading translated medical reports.  Also, once the Panel had a firmer grasp of the existing medical reports, it might require clarification from the Tribunal's consultant specialists.  [5 pages]

The worker injured his low back at work in August 1989.  He was awarded a 15% pension in December 1990.  In November 1991 the worker was getting out of his car when he slipped and sharply twisted his body to grab the car so as to keep from falling.  He felt sharp pain and sought medical treatment.

The worker claimed that he injured his back while lifting his desk to retrieve a small object that had fallen under the desk's drawers.  He stated that this incident occurred one evening after everyone else had gone home.
The worker requested a partial commutation of his 30% pension for debt liquidation.  He sought at least a 50% commutation.

DecKeywords: Hearing loss; Medical opinion (hearing loss) (deterioration after removal from exposure)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a pension for hearing loss.  The worker worked at a paper mill from 1941 until he retired in 1979 at age 65.  He continued to do part-time consulting for the employer until 1981.  Audiograms showed bilateral 25 decibel hearing loss in 1979 and 1982.  In 1983, the hearing loss was 50 decibels in one ear and 30 decibels in the other.

DecKeywords: Credibility (interested witness); Delay (claim); Reactive airways dysfunction syndrome
DecSummary: The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting entitlement to the worker for reactive airways dysfunction syndrome in August 1987.  The worker appealed denial of entitlement to lost time benefits and a pension assessment.

The worker appealed a Hearings Officer decision that the worker was not entitled to benefits for a left ankle problem on the grounds that the diagnosed problem, an aneurysm of the left posterior tibial artery, was not related to the compensable accident.  At the Tribunal hearing, the worker no longer wished to argue the aneurysm issue, but rather claimed that  the problem had always been the joint dysfunction in the worker's ankle that had been treated by a chiropractor at the time of the accident.
The worker slipped and fell and September 1986.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting entitlement for right hip surgery in January 1992.

DecKeywords: Access to worker file, P. D. (issue in dispute) (independent operator)
DecSummary: The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer finding that the claimant for benefits was a worker under the Act, rather than an independent operator.  The claimant objected to the release of the Case Description to the employer on the grounds that it was of no probative value in establishing whether the claimant was self-employed.

DecKeywords: Supplements, transitional provisions (permanent) (retirement); Supplements, transitional provisions (temporary) (participation in rehabilitation)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a compensable injury in March 1986. The worker suffered a back injury in January 1988 and received benefits for one week.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further entitlement after June 1989.

DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for hearing loss on the basis that the worker did not have sufficient noise-induced hearing loss to attract entitlement.

DecSummary: The worker appealed a Reinstatement Officer decision that the Act's re-employment provisions did not apply because the accident employer had less than 20 workers.  The worker argued that the corporate veil should be pierced to show that another company, which had more than 20 workers, was the real employer.  Alternatively, the worker argued that the accident employer would have had 20 workers, if three principals who had personal coverage had been counted.

The plaintiff's representative belatedly sent out a Section 17 Statement to one party and a letter that corrected the plaintiff's affidavit to another party.  The party who received the letter claimed that the change was material and required legal research.  The plaintiff's representative wished to proceed as his witnesses were present.
The hearing was adjourned so that TCO could subpoena witnesses whom the worker was unable to contact.  [4 pages]

Among the issues appealed by the employer was the worker's entitlement to various periods of supplementary benefits under s. 43(9).  The worker cross-appealed with respect to the denial of such benefits on a specific day.  During the relevant period, the worker was employed with the accident employer at a wage loss.  He was receiving both NEL and FEL benefits.  The worker missed short periods of work, on the advice of his doctors, due to flare-ups of his compensable chronic back pain.  The Panel was required to determine whether these sporadic absences attracted payment of supplementary benefits, or whether benefits for these absences were included in the NEL and FEL awards.

The Hearings Officer granted the worker temporary benefits from 1987 to 1988 and directed that the worker be assessed for a pension thereafter.  The worker appealed denial of further temporary benefits.  The worker had not yet been assessed for a pension or considered for supplementary pension benefits.  The hearing was adjourned and the matter referred to the Board for assessment of the worker's pension, including a finding as to when the worker achieved maximal medical rehabilitation.  [4 pages]

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying ongoing entitlement after June 1991, for back disability resulting from a compensable accident in November 1990.  On the evidence, the worker continued to suffer from back pain after June 1991.  The worker was entitled to be assessed for a pension.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for chronic vasomotor rhinitis which the worker related to exposure to fumes in the workplace.  After hearing the evidence, the Panel decided that it required additional medical evidence.  The Panel directed the Tribunal Counsel Office to arrange for an examination by a medical assessor.  [5 pages]

Despite the worker's absence, her representative wished to proceed with the appeal of a decision which reduced the worker's temporary partial benefits to 50%, from the time her vocational rehabilitation services were closed until they were re-opened.  The Panel determined that the worker's presence was necessary to decide her appeal on the true merits and justice of the case.  The hearing was adjourned.  [4 pages]

The worker suffered a low back injury in October 1988.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting only 50% benefits for temporary partial disability from April 1989 to April 1991.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the parties to return to the Board for final decisions on aspects of the case that had not been adjudicated at the Board.  [4 pages]

The worker tripped and fell in March 1986, injuring his back.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting 50% benefits from August 1986 to October 1986 and denying benefits thereafter.

DecKeywords: Pensions (lump sum) (ten per cent pension); Supplements, transitional provisions (temporary) (lay-off)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a back and leg injury in 1987, for which he was awarded a 10% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying commutation of the pension and denying a s. 147(2) supplement from January 1992 to February 1992.

The worker slipped and fell in December 1989, injuring his back.  He was awarded a 15% pension for organic disability.  The worker appealed the level of pension for organic disability, the denial of a pension for non-organic disability and the denial of temporary benefits after February 1993.

DecSummary: The worker was granted a 5% pension in 1986 for hand arm vibration syndrome (HAVS).  It was increased to 7% in 1992.  The worker appealed the level of his pension.
